title: Is There a Low-High-Middle Pattern
statement: Return `true` if there are three positions `i < j < k` with `numbers[i] < numbers[k] < numbers[j]` (the values form a "1-3-2" shape: a small one, then a big one, then a middle one), otherwise `false`.

examples.explanation: The numbers only go up: there is never a smaller number after a bigger one.

hints.nudge: Fix the 'middle' value (the 2) and the 'big' value (the 3) in front of it. Then you only need ONE smaller value even earlier. Scan from the right: what should you remember?
hints.pattern: Scan from right to left with a stack; keep `third`, the largest value that has a bigger value before it (to its left) among those seen; if the current number is smaller than `third`, you found the pattern.
hints.walkthrough: Checking all triples is O(n^3). Going from the right, the stack holds numbers that could play the 'big' part (the 3). When a new number x is bigger than some stack entries, each of those entries has a bigger number (x) to its LEFT and is therefore a valid 'middle' (the 2) for that bigger number; the largest popped entry is the best `third`, because the larger the middle value is, the easier it is to find a smaller number further left. `third` always has a bigger number to its left AND stays to the right of everything still to be read. So when a number x further left is smaller than `third`, the three numbers x, the bigger number and `third` form the pattern in the right order of positions. Each number is pushed and popped at most once: O(n).
